step_back.record: Exact: studies 050-057 (7 versions) ran certify/16e-family identifiers on fresh noise-free 20-state, 3-action, 2-bit-reading worlds; across them only a handful of records decided (050 11730008 at 4M conflicts, 056 12330005, 057 COV_O on one seed). candidates.size_free_guarantee: Rejected: no finite trace rules out every larger machine (Inferred: a larger machine can copy the true machine on every visited state and differ only on states the trace never reached). A guarantee with no declared N is impossible from data alone; the guarantee stays conditional on the declared N.
candidates.noise_at_20_states: Rejected for 058: it would sit on top of an identifier that already fails noise-free at 20 states with 2-bit readings; a noisy version can only decide less.
candidates.forecast_certificate_20f: Rejected on pre-plan evidence (Observed, results/diag-058/preplan_probes): proving that every <=20-state rival agrees on a fixed short word was SAT or did not finish within ~3M conflicts on sealed 057 traces; it costs about as much as identification.
candidates.more_scale20_grinding: Rejected: 7 versions of explorers, budgets and search changes on the same 2-bit target gave no gain.
candidates.reading_width: CHOSEN. Pre-plan probe (Observed, sealed 057 seeds, frozen active14, wall-clock deadline, labels not truth-checked): the same 20-state transition graphs with random 4-bit readings were identified on 4/4 seeds in 36-64 s and with 3-bit readings on 3/4. Inference: hardness at 20 states is driven by information per step, not by state count alone; a sensor with more output bits is a real capability Brute does not have (certify/16e accepts only 2-bit readings).

step_back.honest_framing: This is a TARGET CHANGE (richer observations), not progress on 2-bit 20-state worlds. With 16 codes for 20 states most states are told apart by their reading; a B4 pass shows Brute can certify 20-state machines when the sensor is wide, nothing more. 2-bit scale-20 stays Open.

brand: charcoal and sage; no purple, neon, emoji or gold
question: (A, gain) Does certify/20b (certify/16e with a configurable reading width) decide fresh noise-free 20-state worlds at B 2000000, C 50000 when the readings carry 4 bits, versus the same transition graphs with random 2-bit readings? (B) Does 3 bits already help? (C) Is certify/20b at read_bits 2 exactly certify/16e?

hypotheses.H1: no arm issues a WRONG certificate on 60 records (12 fresh seeds x 5 arms), ID checked from the start state and IDF from the current state against the truth
hypotheses.H2: B4 decides (ID+IDF) >= 6/12 and >= 4 more than B2R on the same seeds
hypotheses.H3: B3 decides >= 4/12 and more than B2R
hypotheses.H4: B4 and B4_b give byte-identical canonical records (conflict-counted, host-independent)
hypotheses.H5: certify/20b at read_bits 2 gives the same record as certify/16e on the same input

design.api: one new module brute/api/certify20b.py (brute.certify/20b): Certifier20B(initial, num_actions, family_bound, read_bits in {2,3,4}, ...), a subclass of certify/16e. Readings are tuples of read_bits entries 0/1/None; m = 2**read_bits codes. Everything else (conflict-counted chunked resume, stop rule, labels, K, encoding) is certify/16e's frozen code, imported, never edited. Host-agnostic: no I/O, threads, subprocess or os.
design.worlds: experiments/worlds_058.py: for seed s, the transitions, start and passive prefix (worlds_026 actions, eps 0) are exactly worlds_050 scale20 for s. Emissions: family scale20 = the original 2-bit emissions; scale20rB (B in 2,3,4) = [rng.randrange(2**B) for q in range(20)] with rng = random.Random(s*11+580+B). Reading of code c with B bits: bit j = (c>>(B-1-j))&1.

arms.B2: scale20 (original 2-bit emissions), read_bits 2: the 057 API16E20 baseline setup at K 400
arms.B2R: scale20r2 (random 2-bit emissions), read_bits 2: the control for the emission RNG
arms.B4_b: B4 again, second pass in reversed seed order (determinism)

design.K_note: K 400 (not 128) because the pre-plan probe used up to 151 extra actions at 3-4 bits; declared before data, same for every arm
design.stop_rule: conflict-only (no host hook); 900 s case guard as a safety net only; any firing fails GDET58
design.workers: one 8-worker pool, max_tasks_per_child 1; job order per seed B4, B3, B2R, B2, then B4_b in reversed seed order
design.truth_label: ID correct iff the model is behaviour-equal to the truth from the start state; IDF correct iff the model from s1 is behaviour-equal to the truth from the true current state; else WRONG. AMB, K_spent and unknown are undecided, not soundness failures
